core_obligations: Retain the construction on printed p.981 that dualizes padded irreducible FI-modules, obtains the maps f^*, and identifies inverse images of the intrinsic hyperplanes H_alpha.

Retain complete Proposition 3.5 and proof (printed pp.981–982): FI generation from finite set-partition data, the tabloid description of the forward map, its cokernel support, the condition on partition parts, and the lift of every relevant flat through preimages.

Retain all three conclusions of Theorem 3.7 and its complete proof (printed p.983), including the Orlik–Solomon tensor-power argument, the numerical i(|lambda|+lambda_1) bounds, and the author distinction between bounds descending to quotients and generation-degree bounds.
Keep exact definitions of partitions, padded representations, FI modules, intrinsic hyperplanes, complements and normal FI-arrangements; no proof-support result is separately counted.
proof_roadmap: Build the intrinsic FI-arrangement using duality and hyperplane pullbacks.
Prove generation and normality with the current set-partition and tabloid/cokernel arguments.
Apply Gadish and FI stability, then derive the quantitative bounds using Orlik–Solomon and tensor powers.
difficulty_reason: The retained current proof must turn the padded irreducible representations into a contravariant geometric arrangement and establish normality of that specific arrangement: it analyzes the forward map on tabloid vectors, identifies the cokernel support, detects which intrinsic hyperplanes can contain it via their partition labels/normal vectors, and lifts the corresponding intersections. This concrete representation-to-arrangement and flat-lifting argument (p.981 construction and full Proposition 3.5 on p.982) remains part of this single principal claim after all listed standard FI/Gadish/Orlik–Solomon inputs are allowed. Theorem 3.7 then propagates the bounded hyperplane generation through tensor powers to character and partition-shape bounds while retaining the quotient caveat. H2 is based on those explicit current obligations, not on the final direct invocation of a stability theorem, terminology or venue.
